components.cost_effect: p additional directions beyond k increase the number of A products from k to k+p and also increase Gaussian generation and orthonormalization work.
components.goal: Capture an approximate range with ell=k+p sample directions.
components.key_estimate: Theorem thm.P082.frobenius bounds E||(I-P_Y)A||_F using the singular-value tail after k and factor sqrt(1+k/(p-1)).
components.name: Gaussian sampling with oversampling
components.operation: Draw Omega, form A Omega and take an orthonormal basis of its range.
components.requires: Selected real Gaussian parameter regime; independent N(0,1) entries and exact products.
transfer_checks: A different sketch law requires replacement of the Gaussian independence, invariance and pseudoinverse-moment analysis.
Approximate products and finite-precision orthogonalization need separate error analysis.
Rank-k truncation and explicit factor formation must retain their own error and access accounting.

limitations.statement: The returned basis does not by itself include Q*A; obtaining explicit approximation factors requires additional access and work.
The linked Theorem supplies an expectation bound for the projection. It supplies neither the same guarantee for rank-k truncation nor an unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower bound.

performance_links.scope_note: Expected Frobenius projection residual for fixed real A, integer k,p>=2, k+p<=min(m,n). Output rank is at most k+p.

variants.cost: Stage A uses ell products with A, n ell Gaussian draws, and orthonormalization. Source Eq.(4.1) estimates T_basic ~ ell n T_rand + ell T_mult + ell^2 m; the QR work is not free. For a basis with d columns, optional B=Q*A can be computed with d products with A* and costs O(dmn) flops for dense A; output factors avoid materializing QB. Optional direct SVD of B and lifting its left vectors cost O(d^2 n) and O(d^2 m), respectively (§5.1, replacing its basis-size symbol by d). These Stage B costs are additional.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.22 Algorithm 4.1, §4.1, Eq.(4.1); pp.29–30 §5.1 and Algorithm 5.1. Rank-deficiency wording above makes explicit the source's instruction to take a basis of range(Y).
variants.name: Real Gaussian range finder in the Theorem 10.5 regime
variants.output: An orthonormal basis Q of range(Y); if d=rank(Y), a basis has d<=ell columns and QQ*=P_Y. The source box writes an m x ell Q; the basis formulation handles rank-deficient Y without assuming rank(A)>=ell. Optional factors represent QB=P_Y A, of rank at most ell; no rank-k truncation is included.
public_inputs: Dimensions m,n and access to products x->Ax
variants.query_and_update: For each column omega_j of Omega, compute y_j=A omega_j; assemble Y=[y_1,...,y_ell]=A Omega. Compute an orthonormal basis Q for range(Y), e.g. by a stable QR-based procedure. There are no adaptive query updates. Optional Stage B: compute B=Q*A separately and represent the approximation by factors (Q,B).
variants.requirements: Exact matrix products and orthonormal basis computation. Selected performance conditions are those of Theorem 10.5. Additional A* or direct matrix access is needed only if forming the optional Stage B factors.
variants.state_and_initialization: For fixed A in R^{m x n}, set ell=k+p. Draw Omega in R^{n x ell} with all entries independent N(0,1). No knowledge of singular vectors or singular values is used to execute the fixed-sample rule.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Choose admissible k,p publicly in advance, use ell=k+p samples, and stop after forming Q. No adaptive tolerance certificate or automatic rank selection is included. Increasing p changes the explicit factor in the linked Theorem and the sampling cost.

use_restrictions: No unrestricted Oracle Complexity claim or automatic rank-k truncation guarantee.
Exact mathematical implementation; stable orthogonalization is advised by §4.1 but no finite-precision error theorem is extracted.
Reference proposal is not Reviewer acceptance or publication. Null dependency revisions are for caller preparation within this batch.

summary: Sample independent Gaussian directions, apply A, and orthonormalize the sampled range; explicit approximation formation has separate access and cost.
title: Gaussian randomized range finder
use_when: Construct an approximate range basis when products with a fixed real matrix are available.
